summary: HomeRise at Mission Bay is a 141-unit, four-story permanent supportive housing project at 410 China Basin St for formerly homeless adults, developed jointly by BRIDGE Housing and Community Housing Partnership with services from HomeRise, and built with modular units fabricated offsite at Factory OS -- HomeRise's first modular project.

milestones.text: HomeRise and BRIDGE Housing (with Community Housing Partnership) selected by OCII to develop Mission Bay South Block 9 as supportive rental housing
Project opens (HomeRise's own project page gives only the bare year; sources do not agree on an exact month -- see open questions)

facts.value: 410 China Basin St (Mission Bay South Block 9)
BRIDGE Housing and Community Housing Partnership (co-developers); services provided by HomeRise
Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects (lead), with associate architects Lowney Architecture and Y.A. Studio
Factory OS (Vallejo, CA), union labor -- HomeRise's first modular project
141 (the architect's own current portfolio page gives 140; not reconciled)
Permanent supportive rental housing (studios) for formerly homeless adults
~92,000-92,535 per HomeRise/the architect; one outlet gives 100,000
Maximum income eligibility is 50% AMI; in practice most residents' income is well below 20% AMI (Social Security-based), with rent set at roughly 30% of resident income
Formerly homeless individuals referred through San Francisco's Adult Coordinated Entry system

4% low-income housing tax credits/tax-exempt bond financing, competitive state tax credits, Federal Home Loan Bank of San Francisco Affordable Housing Program, an OCII loan, California Tax Credit Allocation Committee, California Debt Limit Allocation Committee, National Equity Fund Inc., Wells Fargo, SF Dept. of Homelessness and Supportive Housing, and MOHCD's Local Operating Subsidy Program
GreenPoint Rated Platinum; high-performance envelope and windows; enhanced ventilation; rooftop solar; ground floor elevated for sea-level-rise resilience
U-shaped building around a landscaped courtyard; three wings (one single-loaded, two double-loaded)

open_questions: Exact opening/occupancy month is not confirmed. A 2021 projection said 'as early as January 2022' (Potrero View); HomeRise's own site gives only 'Opened: 2022'; a landscape-architect credit lists the project 'Completed in 2023'; this project's other sources (status.csv) say 'late 2022' per sfchronicle.com, not independently reconfirmed here. Recorded the milestone as the bare year 2022, approximate.
Unit count is 141 in nearly all sources but the architect's own current portfolio page says 140.
Square footage varies: ~92,000 sq ft (HomeRise, the architect) vs. 100,000 sq ft (SF YIMBY) -- not resolved, likely a gross-vs-net difference.

No AMI-specific figure was found tied officially to this project beyond the general permanent-supportive-housing program description; no official OCII/MOHCD underwriting document for Block 9 itself was located.
Could not confirm whether any units are specifically set aside for veterans.

HomeRise's own project page separately lists 'David Baker Architects' and 'James E. Roberts-Obayashi Corp.' under a partners/sponsors list, conflicting with every other source (BRIDGE Housing, the architect's own site, SF YIMBY), which consistently identify Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects and Cahill Contractors. Treated the majority sources as authoritative.
Construction cost figures conflict across sources ($42M construction/$86M total per SF YIMBY, vs. a per-unit figure in Potrero View that implies roughly $54M); not reconciled.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.
